answer: Agents can require each account to earn trust through repeated, randomly timed tasks with scarce, externally verifiable outcomes, rather than accepting self-reported identities. A reputation graph then discounts clusters whose endorsements echo one another but lack links to established participants. A sybil operator must keep many accounts active, pay for real work, and risk detection when their coordination leaves a shared pattern—like opal claims flowing down one river—so fabricating identities is costly, not free.
